about: Questions that lead (N008; OWNER_PRINCIPLES rule 10, his words 'that question is very leading'). Each approved bank question whose right choice is far longer than the others (the classic tell) with a draft that brings every choice to the same short form. The reasoning stays in each item's lesson text. Nothing changes in the bank until he approves an item.
found_by: every approved item in the local bank copy: the right choice at least 1.8x the others' average length and over 25 characters (21 found; the two 'Which principle is this?' items are left as they are: every choice there has the same 'name (detail)' form)

now.q: A stock gaps up on its earnings report on heavy volume and closes strong. By the firm's rulings, what is that day by default?
choices: A Kicker Candle
A High Volume Edge
A Slingshot trigger
An earnings gapper (a Power Earnings Gap), not a Kicker
now.answer: An earnings gapper (a Power Earnings Gap), not a Kicker

now.q: The day before closed red and weak near its low, with a real body. It looked like a failed breakdown out of a clean base. Today, not an earnings day, gapped up and closed strong above that red day's high. Which setup is this?

The Slingshot is intraday; the Kicker is daily
now.answer: The Kicker reverses ONE weak red day on a gap; the Slingshot retakes the average after a MULTI-day pullback and needs no gap

now.q: In the firm's Bull Flag playbook, where does the stop go?
choices: Above the wedge / consolidation high.
Below the 30-minute opening-range low (Day 1), or below the Day 2 volume-support level.
Below the low of the flag. Keep the stop tight, a clean flag should not give much back; a break below the flag low invalidates the continuation thesis.
Below the wedge / consolidation low.
now.answer: Below the low of the flag. Keep the stop tight, a clean flag should not give much back; a break below the flag low invalidates the continuation thesis.

now.q: In the firm's IPO Base playbook, where does the stop go?
choices: Below the lower wick / low of the candle that held the 20-EMA.

Below the breakout day’s low or the most recent tight area; on the faster variant, below the 10/20-day SMA. Because the full base can be wide, anchor the stop to the last tight contraction rather than the deep base low so risk stays within a few percent of entry.
Below the breakout candle low and the 9-EMA, on a strong breakout candle these coincide and give a tight stop.
Below the candle that held the moving averages (intraday version), or below the consolidation low / the MA stack (daily version).

how_applied: On his approval of an item: its choices change at their source (scripts/study/gen_contrasts.py CONTRASTS for the contrast items; a short stop label per playbook in scripts/study/gen_recall.py for the playbook stop items), the bank is regenerated and imported. The question's words never change: an item's id is made from them (scripts/study/_common.item_id), so his approval of the item stands. 'The firm' in a question is already shown as UCT by the display filter (brandWords).
